subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — OptiTech follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Elias Morgan <elias.morgan@optitech.ai>, optitech-devops@optitech.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + two sizing asks (TPS / token mix)

Hi Elias — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and two clarifying asks so we can put together a concrete Dedicated capacity proposal: 

What I heard (please correct if I missed anything):
- Primary use: production inference for an in-product assistant + realtime reranking on search.
- Traffic profile: mostly short requests (single-turn chat + rerank calls), with occasional long-batched jobs for nightly enrichment.
- Target SLO: P95 <= 120ms for chat, P99 <= 350ms for reranking pipeline.
- Initial go-live TPS: 120 sustained TPS, with spikes up to ~500 TPS during peak campaigns.
- Token mix: average request ~90 tokens in / 120 tokens out, but a 10% tail of 800+ tokens for longer chats.
- Security: likely need VPC-only connectivity in future; initial POC can run on Redwood Dedicated with private peering.

Two items we need from you to finalize sizing options:  
1) Can you confirm the percent of synchronous chat vs async batch traffic during peak hours (rough split)? If you have a short traffic sample, please drop it (we discussed optitech_traffic_sample.json).
2) Do you have a firm latency SLO for the reranker (P99) or is the 350ms an aspirational target? That helps us pick between A100-heavy vs A10G-heavy pools.

Next steps from Redwood: we'll draft two Dedicated sizing scenarios (latency-first and cost-efficiency) and bring Karthik into the thread for an engineering runbook (KV cache warmup, batching behavior). Ben will scope procurement support and POC contract terms. 

Attached: OptiTech_token_profile.csv (token mix we sketched during the call).

Thanks — speaking soon.

—Neha

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + two sizing asks (TPS / token mix)

Neha — great summary, thank you. A few clarifications and I attached a 12-hour traffic slice as promised.

Clarifications:
- Traffic split (peak window): ~82% synchronous chat/rerank (real-time), ~18% async batch (enrichment).
- Reranker P99: 320–360ms is our target band; we want to be conservative and aim for <= 350ms on go-live.
- Token distribution: attached sample shows median inbound ~75 tokens, mean ~110, tail at 800+ as mentioned.
- Preferred hardware: our infra team likes A100 (memory helpful for some models), but procurement is pushing for A10G to reduce unit cost. We're flexible if you recommend a hybrid mix.

Attached files: optitech_traffic_sample.json (12-hour capture)

Two questions for you when you produce the scenarios:
1) For the latency-first option, what's the recommended number of NVMe-backed cache nodes vs GPU seats?
2) How much warm-up (KV cache) hit should we expect on a daily cold-start for real-time requests?

Happy to jump on another quick call if that helps.

—Elias

elias.morgan@optitech.ai

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing scenarios (latency-first vs cost-focused) — details and ask list

Elias — thanks for the sample, that helps a lot. Below are two practical Dedicated configurations for OptiTech based on the traffic slice and your P99 targets. I tried to give measurable tradeoffs so Procurement and DevOps can weigh in.

Option A — Latency-first (recommended to hit P99 <= 350ms reliably)
- GPU mix: 4 x A100 (40GB) dedicated GPU seats + 2 NVMe cache nodes (warm KV store for active contexts).
- Expected sustained TPS: ~220 TPS with P95 ~90ms, P99 ~280–340ms for chat; reranking P99 ~320ms.
- Concurrency model: lower per-GPU concurrent streams (optimistic 6–10 streams/GPU) to keep latency stable.
- Cost posture: higher unit cost but lower tail latency; good for launch where UX matters.

Option B — Cost-focused (better $/token at peak)
- GPU mix: 12 x A10G (24GB) + 3 NVMe cache nodes, aggressive batching for rerank jobs.
- Expected sustained TPS: ~420 TPS with P95 ~130–180ms, P99 ~380–500ms for chat; rerank P99 may be above 350ms in tight spikes.
- Concurrency model: more concurrent streams per GPU (18–24 streams/GPU) and larger batch windows to amortize cost.
- Cost posture: ~40–55% lower infra monthly than Option A depending on batching; higher risk on tight tail SLOs.

Hybrid recommendation (practical path): start POC with Option B but reserve a small A100 pool for canary traffic (~40 TPS) to validate P99 behavior. If tail latency exceeds targets during the POC, we can scale in A100 seats or reduce overall concurrency.

Answers to your two questions:
1) NVMe-backed cache nodes: for the sample you provided, 2 NVMe nodes (4 TB each) provide good cache hit rates; if you see a higher working set we recommend moving to 3.
2) KV cache warm-up: typical daily cold-start penalty will impact ~6–12% of requests for the first hour of traffic unless you use pre-warm scripts; with a scheduled pre-warm (crontab job that hits top 200 keys) you can reduce that to ~1–2%.

Ask list for OptiTech so we can produce final sizing and a POC quote: 
- Confirm whether procurement will accept a hybrid pool (A100 + A10G) or require single-family GPUs.
- Approve a 2-week POC window and whether private VPC is required for the POC. POC cost will be credited towards a reserved commitment if you proceed.
- Share any procurement timelines/approval gates (finance contact + proposed contract owner).

I've attached a short PDF with the configuration math and cost delta (redwood_dedicated_config_options.pdf). Karthik — can you draft an engineering checklist (KV pre-warm script, canary routing, telemetry hooks) once Elias confirms the POC window? Ben — can you prepare a POC commercial outline once we get the green light?

—Neha

- POC commercial: 2-week reservation, with full credit toward first-month committed spend if you sign a 12-month Reserved Capacity agreement within 30 days. I'll draft the outline and share as a DocuSign link.
- Can you confirm the finance contact for faster routing? If you share a contact and the procurement cadence we can fast-track approval.

Karthik — over to you for the engineering checklist; can you include the expected rollout steps for private VPC (if OptiTech requires it after POC) and any additional lead times?

Elias — once we have your go-ahead on the POC window and finance contact, I'll share the commercial outline and the PO template. Happy to hop on a 30m call tomorrow afternoon to close logistics.
